place: PAK base near Hesenawa (Hasanawa), Balîsan (Balisan) valley, Herîr (Harir), Hewlêr (Erbil)
summary: Rudaw and The New Region reported that Iranian state forces fired two to four projectiles, which the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK) called ballistic missiles, at a PAK base near Hesenawa in the Balîsan valley on the morning of 21 October; a security source told Rudaw two Hadid-110 drones were used. PAK said the base had been evacuated and no one was hurt.

sources.title: Rudaw: Iran targets Kurdish opposition positions near Erbil
The New Region: PAK says 4 Iranian ballistic missiles targeted Erbil base

place: Around Degaga village, Kosalan area, Serawa (Sarvabad)
summary: ANF and Hawar News, citing a YRK statement, reported that Iranian state forces fired mortars from bases and outposts around Degaga village in the Kosalan area on 20 October. The YRK said it responded and suffered no losses.

place: Deşta Mişarê, Herî Rêş and Kerxenê, Gabar mountain, Şirnex (Şırnak)
impact: Hundreds of oak trees felled around oil fields; risk of desertification
summary: ANF and Yeni Yaşam, citing MA, reported on 20 October that village guards under the supervision of Turkish state soldiers were felling hundreds of oak trees around the Mehmet İrfan Güler and Demir Boğazı oil fields on Gabar mountain. The timber was stacked by the roadside and trucked out via Dihê (Eruh).

place: Seyranbend border gate to Teymiz, Şêweguwêzan and Mîşyawe villages, Başûr–Rojhilat border
impact: About 10 km of concrete wall with watchtowers and a border trench 3 m wide and 4 m deep
summary: ANF, citing RojNews, reported on 21 October that Iranian state forces had built a concrete wall about 10 km long with watchtowers on the border between Başûr and Rojhilat, from the Seyranbend border gate to behind Teymiz and Şêweguwêzan villages, and dug a trench about 3 m wide and 4 m deep up to Mîşyawe village.
